children: In a volatile session on September 9, Indian equity indices ended lower, with the Nifty slipping below the 23,450 mark as selling pressure intensified across most sectoral indices, led by IT and realty stocks.

Amid escalating US-Iran tensions and rising crude oil prices, markets opened lower and remained rangebound through the session. Although a recovery attempt emerged in the afternoon, it failed to sustain, with the benchmarks ending at day’s low.
At close, the Sensex was down 813.35 points or 1.08 percent at 74,764.23, and the Nifty was down 203.60 points or 0.86 percent at 23,431.50, a three-month low.
The broader market also remained under pressure, although it outperformed the benchmark indices. The Nifty Midcap and Nifty Smallcap indices declined 0.5%.

Infosys, HCL Technologies, Tech Mahindra, HDFC Life and Wipro were the biggest Nifty laggards, while Adani Enterprises, Max Healthcare, Adani Ports, Coal India and Tata Steel ended among the top gainers.

On the sectoral front, only the metal and energy indices closed higher, rising 1.8% and 0.6%, respectively. The Nifty IT index was the biggest drag, falling more than 3%, while Nifty Realty declined 2%. Media, FMCG and Private Bank indices shed nearly 1% each.
More than 180 stocks touched 52-week high including TVS Holdings, Solar Industries, Piramal Pharma, Divis Labs, among others. Click to View More

On the other hand more than 120 stocks touched 52-week low, including Voltas, United Breweries, ICICI Lombard, Indiamart Intermesh, JK Lakshmi Cement, IRCTC, Cello World, Dabur India, P&G Hygiene, Godrej Consumer, , among others. Click to View More

Among individual stocks, Adani Ports shares rose nearly 4% post LoA for development and operations of two dry bulk berths at Paradip Port, Odisha. Graphite India rose 15% after graphite electrode price hike announced by US-based GrafTech International, Coforge share price fell 5% after company's chairperson and non-executive independent director O P Bhatt resigned with immediate effect.

Raymond share price shed 5% after board approved fundraising, Innovision share price added 9% after company received a Letter of Award (LoA) worth Rs 243.6 crore and share price of Enviro Infra Engineers surged 5% on contract win worth Rs 189.99 crore from Tata Power Renewable Energy.
The Indian rupee extended its decline for the second consecutive session, slipping past the 95 per dollar mark and closing 28 paise lower at 95.10, compared with the previous close of 94.82.

title: Taking Stock: Markets hit 3-month low as Nifty closes below 23,450; Sensex declines 813 pts
